gaps: Deep-dive documentary coverage of daily life, living costs, and social customs of ordinary Indians across different eras (e.g., Mughal era India, British Raj 1900s).
Lesser-known royal heists, fort vault mysteries, and forgotten treasures of specific Indian princely states backed by archival facts rather than pure rumor.
First-hand micro-histories of Partition and localized freedom struggle incidents beyond standard textbook political timelines.
saturated: Standard textbook colonial history (e.g., basic Vasco da Gama arrival videos - vsNormal 0.01).
Commodity/Object history documentaries without strong royal/mystery angles (e.g., Potato history vsNormal 0.14, Shilajit history vsNormal 0.23).
Non-Indian history or generic world monuments (e.g., Great Wall of China documentary - vsNormal 0.03).
